summary: Argentina is in a quieter stretch under President Milei, but stocks are slipping. The Merval fell 1% to 94,530 on Oct 29, its fourth straight loss, while dollar bonds bounced and country risk eased back under 750 points (Ambito, Infobae). That is still above the 709 seen on Oct 22, so the trend in risk is up. Monthly inflation was 1.9% in September and yearly inflation 33.4%, and the IMF's third review is still open. Energy names ride Vaca Muerta output and oil above $100.
for_you: Argentina is a high risk, high swing market. YPF and VIST ride oil above $100. Keep any trade small, and check the inflation print on Oct 13 first.

On Nov 4 Copom held the Selic at 13.75% in a unanimous vote and ended its cutting cycle, citing a stronger dollar, El Nino and inflation expectations above target (Poder360, Agencia Brasil via Sou Brasilia). About a third of forecasters had expected a cut. The next signals are the December meeting and any fiscal plan from the government.

summary: China and the US have both pushed the trade truce to Jan 10, 2027: on Nov 9 China's commerce ministry extended its pause on the October 2025 rare earth export rules, which were due to return Nov 10, along with other trade countermeasures (Reuters). The White House said Nov 13 that Trump will meet Xi and Putin together on Nov 19 at the APEC summit in Shenzhen (Bloomberg; BBC). Tariffs are still high: about 36.5% on Chinese goods into the US, per a July 2026 Congressional Research Service report. A new irritant: Nvidia's board is probing reports that its CEO was the target of a Chinese intelligence effort, and House chairs want a briefing Nov 18 (CNBC). Mainland stocks stay weak and the October PMI was 49.3; the yuan is near a four year high. On Nov 12 Alibaba fell about 7% after Bloomberg reported it rents Nvidia chips through Singapore based Megaspeed while Commerce finishes rules to block Chinese access to US chips in data centers abroad; Nvidia's CEO resigned the same day and the Senate Banking chair asked him and the Commerce Secretary to testify in December. New on Nov 25: the USTR proposed up to 20% more on most Chinese goods (10% on an annex list, with exemptions), on top of existing duties, and said the rate accounts for last year's Kuala Lumpur truce (USTR). CNBC said it could rise to 40% if Beijing breaks the truce. These are proposals: written comments are due Jan 5, 2027 and hearings start Jan 25, 2027 (USTR), so nothing takes effect before late January. New on Nov 27: mainland stocks jumped after state media read out a government meeting saying policymakers would do more to stop the long slide. The CSI 300 rose more than 4% to 4,063.06, its best day in over two years, and the CSI Semiconductor index rose about 17%, its biggest one day gain on record (CNBC; Wind). October industrial profits rose 20.1% from a year ago, led by electronics and memory (NBS via CNBC). The metals ban pause now runs to Jan 27, 2027 (VOA; Global Times).
for_you: China matters to you mostly through US names that sell there and through memory supply. A stronger yuan helps US exporters' China sales a little. No action; Chinese ADRs are not on the buy zone list.

summary: The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.5% on Oct 29 in a unanimous vote, but said a hike was debated, and markets price about a 67% chance of a hike in December (CNBC, LSEG). Euro area inflation is 3.8%, the highest since September 2023, with energy up 18.8%, and Dutch gas for December jumped to 101.63 euros on Oct 30, the highest since late 2022, with storage near 75% (CNBC). President Lagarde said she will step down on Feb 7, 2027, adding a leadership question to the rate path (CNBC). France's economy shrank 0.1% in Q3 amid unrest and a budget fight, while Shell and BP beat on refining (Insee via CNBC, Reuters). ASML is still the European name that matters most for the AI themes. New on Nov 25: the USTR proposed a 15% tariff on all EU goods, net of normal duties, naming autos, chemicals and pharmaceuticals, and up to 15% on Swiss goods, naming pharmaceuticals and steel (USTR). These are proposals: written comments are due Jan 5, 2027 and hearings start Jan 25, 2027 (USTR), so nothing takes effect before late January.
for_you: A December ECB hike would firm the euro, which helps US holders of European ADRs but hurts exporters. Energy is the pressure point: TTE and Shell gain, while European industry and BUD pay. No European name is a setup; European bank ADRs (SAN, ING) stay a wait.

summary: The US war on Iran is in its eighth month. On Nov 12 the Houthis claimed drone strikes on an Aramco site in Riyadh, the Yanbu refinery and an East West pipeline pumping station; the Saudi led coalition said it downed two drones and no damage was confirmed (House of Saud; The New Arab). Iran's military said four tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz the same day, and Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran. Brent settled up 3.3% at $95.82 (Reuters). On Nov 13 it held just under $96 after the IEA said supply now exceeds demand for the first time since the war began (Invezz). Earlier in the week Brent briefly traded under $90 on deal hopes. New on Nov 26 and 27: Kuwait's army said two Italian nationals were killed in alleged Iranian attacks, which Tehran denied, and Israel said it was ready to strike Iran again even without the US. Trump said victory was at hand but Iran still had every chance to make a deal. Early Friday Brent was about $96.51 and US crude rose 3.0% to $85.75 (CNBC); Saxo had Brent over $97. OPEC meets Sunday Nov 29.
for_you: No oil swings: there are no energy setups on the dashboard. No puts on energy or airlines while Brent moves $4 a day on headlines. A failed Iran deal brings the oil premium back fast and hurts DAL first; a signed one could push Brent lower again.

summary: Foreign money is coming back to India as it leaves the AI trade. Foreign investors bought more than Rs 1 lakh crore of Indian stocks in November, the first month they crossed that mark, after selling from May to October (Business Today; IndiaIPO). On Nov 19 the Sensex rose 990 points to 83,022 and the Nifty 286 points to 25,514 (Business Today). On Nov 20, while the S&P 500 fell 3.7%, the INDA fund rose to 52.90 on 1.71 times its normal volume (Massive). The RBI raised its repo rate to 5.50% on Oct 7 and may hike again in December. Cheaper oil helps an oil importer. A 10% US tariff still applies to most Indian goods. New on Nov 25: the US Trade Representative proposed tariffs of up to 25% on all Indian goods, or 17% if India signs a trade deal, and its India report names pharmaceuticals and medical devices first (USTR). These are proposals: written comments are due Jan 5, 2027 and hearings start Jan 25, 2027 (USTR), so nothing takes effect before late January.
for_you: INDA closed exactly at its 53.20 breakout level on Nov 25 on 11.8 million shares (Massive): volume passed, but a close at the level is not a close over it. With a 25% tariff now proposed and drug makers named, wait for a close over 53.20 on 9,700,000+ shares before any entry. RDY: no new swing entry until the tariff path is clearer.

summary: The Bank of Japan held at 1.25% on Oct 30 in an 8 to 1 vote, with one member wanting 1.5%, and for the first time since 2013 called inflation 'generally consistent' with its 2% target (CNBC). All 16 economists in a CNBC survey expect the BOJ to set up a hike in December or January. The Nikkei fell 2.12% to 63,290.11 on Oct 30, ending a four day run, as US tech results hit chip names: Advantest fell 5.43%, Tokyo Electron 3.93% and SoftBank 4.66% (CNBC). The yen is near 157 per dollar, still weak enough to help exporters. Higher rates help the big banks. On Nov 13 the yen weakened past 160 per dollar, a level that came before intervention twice this year, and the vice finance minister warned moves were too rapid (MLQ). New on Nov 25: the USTR proposed tariffs of up to 15% on all Japanese goods, net of normal duties, and said it accounts for the existing framework deal (USTR). The Nikkei 225 fell 2.88% that day (CNBC). These are proposals: written comments are due Jan 5, 2027 and hearings start Jan 25, 2027 (USTR), so nothing takes effect before late January.
for_you: No action. A December BOJ hike is now the base case, which can lift the yen and jolt US tech for a day or two. EWJ closed at 94.94 on Oct 29 (Massive); no Japan name is a setup.

summary: The peso weakened 1.2% to about 18.86 per dollar on Oct 29 as strong US growth and inflation revived bets on another Fed hike (TMGM). Banxico holds at 6.50%, and Deputy Governor Galia Borja called that a 'good monetary position' with inflation moving toward 3%, though 'the job is not yet done' (TMGM). Q3 GDP is due Oct 30, with forecasts of 0.7% growth on the quarter and 2.5% on the year. The USMCA was not renewed in July and moved to annual reviews, so trade rules for cars and factories stay uncertain. A weaker peso cuts the dollar value of Mexican profits but lowers costs for companies that make goods in Mexico and sell in the US. New on Nov 25: the USTR left Mexico out of its 14 new Section 301 tariff proposals and said it has not made a determination on Mexico for now (USTR). EWW rose 2.0% to 73.34 and CEMEX 3.8% (Massive).
for_you: A weaker peso and rate cuts help the airport stocks (ASR, PAC) more than consumer names. Nothing here is a setup today. Watch only if you want Mexico exposure.

summary: Korea is a memory chip market, and it swings hardest on AI news. After the US midterms raised fears of limits on AI data centers, the KOSPI fell 5.28% on Nov 5 and another 6.02% to 5,059.69 on Nov 6, when a circuit breaker halted trading three minutes after the open; SK hynix fell 10.44% and Samsung 6.35% (Korea Herald). The selloff is about whether AI spenders keep paying and who owns these stocks, not about current memory demand: both companies have said HBM supply stays tight into 2028. On Nov 11 the KOSPI rose 2.6% to 5,375.36 after CoreWeave's results (CNBC). On Nov 23 the KOSPI fell as much as about 5.8% intraday after a 5.21% drop on Nov 20, and Seoul said it is preparing its stabilization fund, unused since 2008 (Korea JoongAng Daily). New on Nov 25: the USTR proposed tariffs of up to 15% on all Korean goods, naming autos, chips and petrochemicals (USTR). The KOSPI fell more than 6% that day as the AI sell off resumed (CNBC). These are proposals: written comments are due Jan 5, 2027 and hearings start Jan 25, 2027 (USTR), so nothing takes effect before late January. New on Nov 27: the KOSPI rose 4.34% to 4,915.68 and the Kosdaq 8.13% as buyers came back to chip stocks (CNBC), with reports that Seoul may enlarge its stabilization fund (Saxo).
for_you: No Korea or memory trades. EWY fell 13.46% to 131.65 and the SK hynix ADR 13.40% on Nov 5 (Massive). Wait for a calm week and a base.

summary: Taiwan's story is the AI chip boom. On Oct 15 TSMC reported Q3 revenue of $46.72 billion, up 41.2%, and guided Q4 to $52.3 to $54.3 billion, saying AI demand is far above supply. But investors now doubt the spenders will keep paying, and after the US midterms raised fears of limits on data centers, the TSMC ADR fell 10.78% to 353.10 and EWT 11.54% to 85.88 on Nov 5 (Massive). TSMC's own guidance has not changed. The main local risks remain China-Taiwan tension or US chip tariffs; no new tension was found this week. New on Nov 25: the USTR proposed tariffs of up to 15% on all Taiwanese goods, naming electronics, chips and telecom gear (USTR). TSM fell 2.0% to 342.34 (Massive). These are proposals: written comments are due Jan 5, 2027 and hearings start Jan 25, 2027 (USTR), so nothing takes effect before late January.
for_you: No new Taiwan puts or buys while the chip selloff runs. This is a price problem, not a business problem, until TSMC's monthly sales say otherwise.
